title: Sufficiency of Manpower at Child Protection Service
what_it_is: Sufficiency of Manpower at Child Protection Service

sections.label: CPO hiring and caseload
sections.summary: CPS is hiring more CPOs as caseloads average 40 cases each, affected by retirements, recruitment and training time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: CPS is in the process of hiring more CPOs to meet evolving needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand the caseload currently is at an average of 40 cases for each CPO, which is quite a lot, considering there are really difficult cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Could I check what the target number of CPOs is?

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: I trust the Member would agree with me that, actually, the situation is a function of several factors, one of which is the number of CPOs retiring or leaving service prematurely; two, our ability to recruit more CPOs; and three, there is a lag in time due to the need for professional and proper training for our CPOs.

sections.label: CPO recruitment and retention
sections.summary: The speaker says CPOs are supported, recruitment and retention are being ramped up, but no firm target can be committed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: We salute our CPOs, they are doing good work and we want to support them so that they have every chance to do their work well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: But given the compendium of the three factors that we are talking about, we are trying to ramp up recruitment and, at the same time, retain our officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: So, I am afraid I cannot commit to a very firm and hard target for the Member.

sections.label: Caseload benchmark and officer targets
sections.summary: The speaker hopes for a caseload benchmark and officer target numbers, agreeing 40 cases may be too high.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: So, I hope we can set some benchmark in terms of the number of cases an officer can take and also have some target numbers in terms of the number of officers we need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: I can agree that 40 is perhaps a tad high.

sections.label: Reducing CPO caseload
sections.summary: The speaker thinks 40 cases is too high and is trying to lower the caseload, but no magic number exists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: So, I hope the Member can see where I am coming from.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: I also think that 40 is a little bit too high.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: We are trying to bring that number for the caseload down, but I do not think we can arrive at a magic number.
